extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists and fiction writers (readers of a craft blog)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical checklist for crafting a novel that covers five foundational elements (structure, character arc, theme, setting, point of view) and a detailed three-act beat schema with approximate percent positions to evaluate pacing and placement of major beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure / Three-Act Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Three Acts: Setup, Conflict, Resolution; Three Major Plot Points: First Plot Point (~25%), Midpoint (~50%), Third Plot Point (~75%); Two Pinch Points: First Pinch Point (~37%), Second Pinch Point (~62%); A strong Hook in the opening; A strong Climax and Resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weiland provides a concrete beat schema with approximate positions to use evaluatively. Beat positions: Hook (1%), Inciting Event (12%), First Plot Point (25%), First Pinch Point (37%), Midpoint/Second Plot Point (50%), Second Pinch Point (62%), Third Plot Point (75%), Climax (88%), Climactic Moment (98%), Resolution (99%). Use this to check a draft: verify each beat exists and is placed roughly where indicated; missing beats or misplaced beats diagnose pacing or structural problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Arc
rubrics_metrics.description: The protagonist needs: A 'Lie They Believe' (the false worldview rooted in a past wound), A 'Truth' (the new worldview the story will lead them to), A 'Want' (externally driven, sourced from the Lie), A 'Need' (internal truth resolved by accepting the Truth), A 'Ghost' (the past wound that produced the Lie), A 'Characteristic Moment' (an opening scene that crystallizes who they are at the start).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character arc is built from these interlocking elements: the Ghost causes the Lie; the Want propels external action; the Need is the interior change the story forces; the Characteristic Moment establishes starting point. Ensure the arc moves the character from Lie toward Truth through plot events and that Want and Need are aligned/conflicted in ways that drive growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme should emanate from character actions rather than be stated; it must connect directly to plot (embedded, not appended); it should argue a complex moral position rather than a simplistic good-vs-evil stance; it should be echoed (but not repeated) by subplots and supporting characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether scenes and character choices dramatize the thematic idea instead of telling it. Check that subplot beats and supporting-cast arcs reinforce a nuanced thematic argument without blunt repetition or didactic statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting must matter to the plot as a catalyst rather than merely a backdrop; it should possess historical backstory that enriches credibility; it should influence the supporting cast organically; it should create atmosphere that reinforces theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use setting elements to shape plot choices and character behavior. Verify the world has verifiable details and history that inform stakes and motivations, and that environmental/atmospheric choices support the story's thematic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose narrator(s) strategically (typically the protagonist); decide narrative distance (deep POV vs. distant); decide tense (past vs. present); maintain voice consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about POV, distance, and tense should serve character intimacy and thematic emphasis. Ensure chosen POV is sustained consistently and that shifts (if any) are deliberate, clear, and motivated by story needs rather than convenience.
